newsitem.title: UK: UK's Brown setS 2.5% target for RPIX.
newsitem.headline: UK's Brown setS 2.5% target for RPIX.

text.p: British Chancellor of the Exchequer Gordon Brown on Thursday set a target of 2.5 percent for annual underlying inflation (RPIX).

In a letter to Bank of England Governor Eddie George, Brown said if RPIX moved away from the target in more than one percentage point in either direction, he would expect an open letter from the Governor explaining why.

"The thresholds do not provide a target range," Brown said in the letter to George. "Their function is to define the points at which I shall expect an explanatory letter from you (George) because the actual inflation rate is appreciably away from its target."

A government source said the Treasury wanted underlying inflation to hit 2.5 percent every month. "We want inflation to be 2.5 percent every month," the source said. "We won't tolerate month by month by month, inflation missing the target with no explanation."
The previous Conservative government first set a 2.5 percent target for annual RPIX. But until the last two months, it had stuck above that target since late 1994.
